Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the West Indies reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and Tagenarine Chanderpaul will open the innings for West Indies. Mohammed Siraj will start with the new ball for India. Here we go...
.... FOURTH INNINGS...

UPDATE - 1.01 am IST (7.31 pm GMT, the previous day) - Uh oh! The Indian players and the two West Indies openers were getting ready to come out on the field but the heavens have opened up. Only the strip has been covered for now, so hopefully this should not be a lengthy delay. Just as we type, the sun has peeked through the clouds and the West Indies run chase should not be far away.

On the flip side, West Indies have their backs against the wall now and might have to play for survival in the remaining time in the Test. The hosts found themselves losing their last five wickets in the first hour and surrendered a lead of 183 runs. Moreover, they were taken to the cleaners by the Indian openers and failed to keep the runs in check. At no point, they were able to dry up the runs and now have a mountain ahead to climb. The first task for the West Indies batting unit will be to see off the remaining passage of play on Day 4 without losing many wickets. Can Kraigg Brathwaite and Co. show up for the fight? Let's find out. Back in a bit for the chase.

Right then, India have declared their second innings at the score of 181! They have set West Indies a target of 365 runs to chase and level the series! Having done exceptionally well to wrap the West Indies innings in the first hour, India took that momentum into their batting effort. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal took no time to get off the blocks and got their side off to an aggressive start. Both openers scored entertaining fifties before departing on either side of the first rain interruption. Ishan Kishan and Shubman Gill carried the momentum forward with the former going full throttle towards the end to bring up his fifty.

Some innovation now from the young wicket-keeper! This is bowled full and outside the off pole. Ishan Kishan gets across the stumps and gets down on one knee to swat it into the leg side. The ball goes high into the air and lands in the vacant deep square leg region. The batters take a couple of runs and the camera pans towards Rohit Sharma who is calling his batters into the dressing room.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Tea session of Day 4. Blue skies greet the two umpires and players as they make their way out to the middle. Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan will resume their innings for India and will look to go hard at the bowling from the word go. Shannon Gabriel will start the proceedings with the ball for West Indies. Let's play...
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

Just three overs were bowled in the afternoon session but a lot happened as Jomel Warrican dismissed Yashasvi Jaiswal in the first over after Lunch. India added 20 runs with Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan at the crease and the lead of 301 runs. There is a high possibility that India may choose to declare much sooner than they would have liked and will need to consider the fact that rain could play a further part in this game. West Indies have an opportunity to save this Test match and their batters will need to apply themselves when asked to bat. If the Windies are given a window of opportunity to chase down this target and they play with positive intent, we could be in for a cracker of a game. Do join us at 12.15 am IST (6.45 pm GMT, the previous day) to find out how the final session of Day 4 pans out.

UPDATE - 11.56 pm IST (6.26 pm GMT) - So the official news is that Tea has been taken and we will have one session of 3 hours and 15 mins up until stumps. The latest up until when we can continue Day 4 is 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, the previous day) with a maximum of 48 overs left.

UPDATE - 11.46 pm IST (6.16 pm GMT) - The rain has stopped and the covers are being rolled up once again. The umpires have made their way out onto the field and are having a look around. The drainage here has been simply outstanding as the puddles seem to be drying up the moment the rain stops. We should hopefully have a start time soon. It has been decided that the game will resume at 12.15 am IST (6.45 pm GMT, the previous day) as the ground is being prepared for action. Stay tuned...

UPDATE - 11.27 pm IST (5.57 pm GMT) - We do not intend to dampen your spirits but the rain has returned. The ground staff though saw it coming and had put the covers back on before the arrival of rain. It is a steady drizzle as both sets of players chatter away in their respective dressing rooms. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 11.02 pm IST (5.32 pm GMT) - Some positive news! The rain has subsided and the covers are being gradually taken off by the ground staff. Considering the puddles formed in the outfield, it should take some time to dry up those areas. The sun is out though which is a positive sign. Stick around as we should have news regarding the resumption soon.

UPDATE - 10.52 pm IST (5.22 pm GMT) - Live pictures show that it is raining heavily at the moment and the water has started to accumulate in the outfield. Looks like we are in a long delay. Stay tuned for further updates.

It has started drizzling and the ground staff waste no time to cover the strip. This stop-and-start in play is hampering India's momentum a bit. That said, their lead is now 301 runs with around five sessions of play remaining in the game. Let's hope the weather clears up soon and that this is a brief delay.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get underway in the post-Lunch session of Day 4. Out come the two umpires, followed by the West Indies players. They are joined by Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill. West Indies are starting with spin as Jomel Warrican has the ball in hand. Here we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 2 ...

UPDATE - 10.16 pm IST (4.46 pm GMT) - Good news, folks! It has stopped raining and the sun is out as well which is a good sign. The ground staff have removed the covers off the square and the West Indies players are seen warming up near the ropes. The two Indian batters, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill are waiting just outside the boundary as well, which means we should be resuming anytime from now.

UPDATE - 9.50 pm IST (4.20 pm GMT) - The second session was scheduled to begin right now but it is raining quite heavily once again. The downpour had subsided and the groundstaff had removed the centre patch to work on the strip but they have brought the covers back on now. We will bring you further updates soon.

As far as West Indies are concerned, it was a disappointing session for them. When the two overnight batters, Alick Athanaze and Jason Holder walked to resume their innings, the game was heading towards a draw but what unfolded was a collapse of epic proportions. They were rocked early as they lost Alick Athanaze in the first over of the day. It went from bad to worse for the hosts as Holder followed Athanaze into the hut soon after. The West Indies tail simply had no answers against the new ball brilliance of Mohammad Siraj  With the ball, they were absolutely blown away by the onslaught from Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma. Moreover, they were made to pay hard by the Indian skipper, having dropped him twice. Shannon Gabriel did redeem himself by accounting for Sharma but the damage had already been done. Kraigg Brathwaite and Co. will look to regroup during the Lunch interval and come out with a renewed vigour. Can West Indies manage to keep the runs in check in the second session? We shall find out as the post-Lunch session resumes in 40 minutes' time.

SESSION SUMMARY: 124 runs, 19.4 overs and 6 wickets. An entertaining session of Test cricket comes to an end! The visitors ticked all boxes in the first session and find themselves in a commanding position at Lunch on Day 4. With the wicket visibly on the slower side, India needed early breakthroughs with the new ball to break the resistance of the West Indies batters. Playing in his debut Test, Mukesh Kumar provided his side with an early scalp of the impressive-looking Alick Athanaze. From the other end, Mohammed Siraj was even more impressive and for rid of the other overnight batter, Jason Holder. He never looked back and simply ran through the tail of the visitors. With his best figures in an innings of Test cricket, he put India in the driver's seat. Having taken a lead of 183 runs, the visitors had the license to go after the bowling from the start. Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal came out with their version of 'Bazball' and signalled their intentions straight away. Both batters raced to their respective fifties before the India skipper was caught two runs short of the century stand.

UPDATE - 9.09 pm IST (3.39 pm GMT) - Uh oh! The trend of a wicket bringing about rain has continued on Day 4! This sudden shower has forced the ground staff to make their way out to the middle with the covers. With just about 20 minutes of play remaining in this extended first session, the umpires have decided to take an early Lunch!
